loader.label: Gemini CLI

start.why: Gemini CLI context docs (docs/cli/gemini-md/): GEMINI.md is collected from the working directory upward through parent directories until the first directory holding a boundary marker (.git by default) or home
Gemini CLI context docs: the user-global ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md opens the concatenation, before any project file

alsoReads.what: the context file under another name — settings.json context.fileName, a string or an array
alsoReads.why: Gemini CLI configuration docs: context.fileName renames the context file (a string or an array), so an installation listing AGENTS.md there reads AGENTS.md as its GEMINI.md

alsoReads.what: GEMINI.md (or the renamed context file) in subdirectories below the working directory
alsoReads.why: Gemini CLI context docs: directories a tool touches are scanned for a context file up to a trusted root, bounded by context.discoveryMaxDirs (200) - not at session start

loader.order: user-global ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md first, then the project chain general to specific - project-root side first (upward traversal stops at the first directory holding a boundary marker, .git by default) down through each directory to the working directory - then just-in-time files a tool touch discovered; the whole result is one concatenation with origin separators
loader.capNote: no byte cap is published for the merged Gemini CLI context (checked 2026-10-26)

imports.why: Gemini CLI context docs: @path imports resolve relative or absolute to a maximum depth of 5, with cycles prevented by skipping files already on the stack

loader.nested: general to specific, all loaded — unlike Codex, every context file on the walk contributes; a nearer file cannot hide a parent one, it just concatenates after it; subdirectory files wait for a tool touch
loader.skillsNote: no project skill directory is documented for Gemini CLI; extensions are the distribution mechanism, and they are tooling not context

hooks.verified: Gemini CLI hooks reference (geminicli.com/docs/hooks/reference/, read 2026-10-26): a project .gemini/settings.json carries a top-level hooks object whose events are arrays of {matcher, hooks:[{type:"command",command,timeout? (milliseconds)}]} — the same shape Claude and Codex use; BeforeTool denies with {decision:"deny",reason}, BeforeAgent and AfterTool inject via hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext

agents.verified: Gemini CLI subagents docs (geminicli.com/docs/core/subagents, read 2026-10-30): project subagents are markdown files with name and description frontmatter under .gemini/agents/

mcp.verified: Gemini CLI configuration docs (docs/reference/configuration/, read 2026-10-26): a project .gemini/settings.json (a user ~/.gemini/settings.json merged behind it, objects merged key by key) carries a top-level mcpServers object whose entries name a command, a url or an httpUrl

loader.verified: Gemini CLI context and configuration docs (geminicli.com/docs/cli/gemini-md/ and docs/reference/configuration/, read 2026-10-26) — settings live at project .gemini/settings.json and user ~/.gemini/settings.json, merged for objects; the context is user ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md plus the context file (GEMINI.md unless context.fileName renames it, an array is allowed) from the working directory upward through parents to the first .git or home, with @path imports to depth 5; server registration is the mcpServers object in those same settings files; no byte cap is published
loader.note: The configuration reference this table once recorded as 404ing is live again as of 2026-10-26, which is why the row is full instead of thin. What still shapes a byte count is the pair of absences the docs confirm rather than deny: no cap, and no promise that AGENTS.md is read at all — context.fileName decides that, and it may name anything.
